composition_selection.model_selection: train_arm selects the checkpoint by dev balanced accuracy over all 16 dev graphs, 4 of which are composition; composition labels therefore influenced checkpoint selection even though no composition graph contributes training gradients.

determinism_checks.interpretation: Same exact SAP -> same 35-d feature -> same encoder output -> same hard argmax, so every concept is a deterministic coarsening of SAP. Consequences: cross_base_consistency=1.0 is guaranteed up to tie-breaking, and I(concept;label|SAP)=0 is guaranteed by construction; neither is independent evidence of cross-base semantic generalisation.

hungarian.definition: contingency_stats matched_purity = linear_sum_assignment over the concept x SAP count matrix, i.e. each concept is matched to at most one exact SAP and each SAP to at most one concept; unmatched mass scores zero. Many-to-one role abstraction is therefore punished in proportion to how many distinct exact SAPs a role spans.

metric_audit.key_sap_purity_definition: sub = patches whose SAP string is in the key set (any family, any split); dominant_share = share of sub assigned to the single most frequent concept. There is no SAP-to-concept matching and no recall term.

role_purity_coverage_confusion.notes: coverage = share of test patches whose concept has train support for that role key; accuracy_covered = accuracy restricted to that subset. MI/nmi(concept;role) measures how much role information survives in the 16-prototype code on the test split; MI/nmi(feature;role) is the same for the raw 35-d input, i.e. the information available before the bottleneck (both on the same test sample, so MI(concept;role) <= MI(feature;role) by data processing). concept_purity_test reports, per concept, the share of its test patches matching its train-majority role (purity) next to the per-role recall above. role_cross_base_dominant_concept_agreement is the role-level analogue of the frozen SAP-level cross_base_consistency (which is deterministic by construction).

role_semantics.taxonomy_notes: role_element = multiset of special elements in the patch (coarse statistic). single_atom_* = only patches with exactly one special atom; global atom role includes 'ring' (not observable from a radius-1 patch when the ring is > 3), the local version replaces ring/chain by the locally observable closure flag, the rich version adds the neighbour-element multiset. single_ring_triangle_visible distinguishes patches where the triangle is inside the patch from atoms globally in a triangle whose closure is not visible.
